runners_data.name: Hemustbeanangel
runners_data.note: Hold-up style dropping back to 7f from 6f debut wins, trainer Roger Teal in modest form (1/10 in 14 days); all three career runs on Good ground suit today's soft less clearly, and from OR 65 needs more than she has shown in three runs finishing 3-3-9.

runners_data.name: Son Of A Fish
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard at 2/52 in 14 days is cold, and this hold-up runner steps up to 7f where his 3rd at the trip on Good is his best evidence; soft ground adds an unknown but the trip suits, and Joe Leavy must find a run from the rear in a congested field.

runners_data.name: Arctic Tsar
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Clive Cox sends him up sharply in trip from 6f (three runs all at 6f), and the soft going is a new test; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that he's being asked to operate in a front-running role that may not be fully natural, yet the uncontested lead is a tangible race-shape asset here.

runners_data.name: Bossy Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's juvenile has form figures of 9-8-5-5 and has been off 46 days — the longest absence in the field; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position because the rear is congested, meaning her true closing run may be compressed, and she lacks the form to compensate.

runners_data.name: Fortunate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's runner is the only horse in the field with a win at 7f (1st at 7f/Standard), and a fifth on Soft last time gives her the clearest soft-ground evidence in the field; a natural hold-up runner at OR 63, she arrives 35 days fresh and her sim-going record (1 from 8, 0 wins, 0 places) is modest but the trip and conditions suit better than most.

runners_data.name: Perfect Hope
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's gelding has a 2nd at 7f on a Standard surface and wears headgear, showing he can travel prominently; OR 61 with a 0W0P record in similar going (1/4) means his placed form is encouraging but he must convert, and Rob Hornby's tactical read from just off the pace is his clearest route to relevance.

runners_data.name: Honeymoon Bear
runners_data.note: Joseph Parr's juvenile has form of 7-4-4, all at 6f, and steps up markedly in trip to 7f on soft — an untested combination; a genuine hold-up runner housed in midfield on the map due to the rear being over-subscribed, meaning Jack Mitchell may struggle to find his preferred position in a field with many like-minded rivals.

runners_data.name: Hamdani Mokhater
runners_data.note: James Horton's runner has the deepest form profile at this trip — 2nd and 3rd both over 7f on Good, with headgear worn — and only 12 days since last run keeps him sharp; displaced to midfield on the map despite being a hold-up type, but his 7f record gives him a strong trip argument that the others around him cannot match.

runners_data.name: Coul Blue
runners_data.note: Michael Dods sends this hold-up runner down from the north at OR 58, wearing headgear, with a 3rd at 7f on Good as his best run; mapped to midfield because true closing positions are over-filled, Tom Eaves must navigate the compression and the soft going is less certain than his Good-ground form suggests.

runners_data.name: King Of Persia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's juvenile is 53 days off the track — longest layoff in the field — and all three runs resulted in 6th-7th-7th finishes, all on Good going over 6-7f; Joanna Mason has a rail position and the horse is lowest-rated in the field at OR 57, a genuine hold-up type whose map position overstates proximity to the pace he will actually run.

races.paceDynamic: Arctic Tsar is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead from the other nine runners, Rossa Ryan can dictate a controlled, unchallenged tempo on soft ground over seven furlongs — a setup that typically produces a slowly-run early pace and a stamina-testing, gruelling finish. Perfect Hope is the only other horse likely to press forward with any conviction, giving Arctic Tsar company but not a battle, so the pace should be sustainable rather than punishing. The soft going amplifies the tactical advantage of those who can settle close to the pace and travel well, rather than closers who face a rising, energy-sapping track from the rear. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can be produced in the run from midfield to challenge into a modest pace — but the critical caveat is that Bossy Angel, Honeymoon Bear, Hamdani Mokhater, Coul Blue and King Of Persia are all genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed in the map because this field contains more rear-running horses than can practically find their natural position; of those, Hamdani Mokhater (best form figures at this trip, second and third at 7f) and Fortunate (a winner at 7f on a testing surface) are best-placed to secure a useful pitch and deliver a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Arctic Tsar Controls, Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Arctic Tsar settles comfortably in front and Rossa Ryan controls the tempo to suit, slowing the race to a crawl before quickening.
scenarios.body: Arctic Tsar has done all his recent racing at 6f and steps up in trip, but a gentle gallop on soft ground suits a horse who can conserve energy and produce a kick; the sole front-runner role with no pressure is a significant asset here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive, Leader Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and the hold-up horses find enough room to mount a late challenge on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop brings the midfield closers right into contention approaching the final two furlongs, and on soft going the track becomes attritional enough to stop a front-runner who has had it too easy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Perfect Hope Presses, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Hope pushes the pace and forces Arctic Tsar to run more freely, creating a more genuine gallop that tests stamina.
scenarios.body: Rob Hornby can sit just off the leader and exploit any weakness, while the stronger pace paradoxically brings the race to a prominent racer who travels well; Perfect Hope's 2nd at 7f on a Standard surface suggests he handles the trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so slow that the entire field compresses into a tight bunch turning for home, producing a scramble.
scenarios.body: Soft ground causes erratic running lines in a congested finish, with jockey positional skill becoming the decisive factor; in such a finish, hold-up horses squeezed wide or blocked are disadvantaged regardless of ability.

watchPoints.text: Arctic Tsar is the only horse guaranteed the lead — if Rossa Ryan settles him comfortably and the pace is minimal, he controls the entire race shape and his uncontested advantage is the single biggest tactical factor in this field.

Hamdani Mokhater is a hold-up runner genuinely mapped away from his natural position; if Daniel Muscutt cannot find a clear run in a congested midfield group on soft ground, his best form at this trip counts for nothing regardless of class.

Perfect Hope (headgear, prominent style) is the only horse likely to apply any pressure to Arctic Tsar — if Rob Hornby elects to press from the front, the entire pace scenario shifts and closers gain more opportunity than the current map suggests.

At least five genuine hold-up horses (Bossy Angel, Honeymoon Bear, Hamdani Mokhater, Coul Blue, King Of Persia) will be competing for the same finishing positions; watch for traffic problems in the final two furlongs as they converge from the same angle on a soft, tiring track.

Fortunate's run on Soft going (5th last time) is the clearest evidence of any hold-up runner handling today's conditions — watch whether Oliver Carmichael can produce her from a better position than her natural rear-of-field berth suggests.

races.name: Dale Hall And Hickman Associates Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ezra Cee
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse trained by Derek Shaw, absent 278 days — a significant fitness concern; best form on Flat at 6f rather than today's minimum 5f, and Staminaside form figures suggest stamina rather than pace; layoff makes reliability questionable.|

runners_data.name: Staniel Cay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Grant Tuer (1 winner from 9 in 14 days, active yard) who won over this exact trip on soft going — the one runner in the hold-up camp whose similar-going form actually reads positively; 22 days fresh and stable in form, Oliver Stammers takes the ride.|

runners_data.name: Our Planet
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up type with a deeply uninspiring record of 0 wins and 0 places from 13 similar-ground runs; Michael Keady's charge has finished 6th or worse in all six recent 5f starts and gives no indication the trip or ground will unlock improvement today.|

runners_data.name: Act Of Violence
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes over on this Tony Carroll five-year-old who is wearing a tongue-tie; won over 6f on Good and placed over this trip recently, but similar-going stats (0W0P from 15) temper enthusiasm — prominent style suits the race shape well regardless.|

runners_data.name: Knicks
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby five-year-old wearing a tongue-tie; genuinely a hold-up horse by nature but this field has too many closers for all to find their preferred rear position — Joanna Mason will likely find Knicks racing more prominently than ideal, discounting its chance under the redistributed tag.|

runners_data.name: Jojo Rabbit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's veteran, 8 years old and lightly rewarded in recent starts; a true closer by inclination that the pace map has shifted into midfield — Tom Eaves will have to improvise its position in a race where natural hold-up ground is crowded, and form figures on this trip are modest.|

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's visor-wearing three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner; Rossa Ryan should get a soft lead on Good to Soft, and while 0W1P from 7 similar-ground starts is a flag, the race shape is tailor-made for an uncontested front-runner who can control fractions.|

runners_data.name: Toptime
runners_data.note: Roy Bowring's eight-year-old won over 5f on Soft last time out (form 1) and has placed on this going before — the most directly relevant recent form in the prominent-tracking group; Alistair Rawlinson rides and similar-going stats (1W1P from 15) suggest soft ground is genuinely within range.|

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Michael Appleby wearing a hood; form figures on similar ground read 0W2P from 8 runs with a recent 7/9 start sequence — Stevie Donohoe takes the ride on a horse that drops slightly in class but whose 5f turf form has been modest throughout.|

runners_data.name: Sergeant Mayer
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's five-year-old actually won over 5f on Good going (most recent winning run) but the field surplus of hold-up horses means Alex Jary (3) will likely find this one squeezed out of its preferred finishing position; style-fit discount applies and similar-going record shows only a single place from 15 attempts.|

runners_data.name: Just King High
runners_data.note: Sean D Bowen takes over on Ross Burdon's four-year-old, equipped with both blinkers and a tongue-tie; OR of 45 makes this the lowest-rated runner in the field, and although repositioned into midfield on the map, it is a natural closer by inclination — an inexperienced jockey pairing and big weight disadvantage compound the challenge.|

races.paceDynamic: Black Missile is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner sprint and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, Rossa Ryan should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Soft ground — a tempo that keeps the race together rather than stringing it out. Act Of Violence, Toptime and Overbudget are all prominent-tracking types who will press close to the pace, meaning the race will be run in a compact, processional shape with little bunching at the rear. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the back: Knicks, Jojo Rabbit, Sergeant Mayer and Just King High are genuine closers who will find themselves shuffled into midfield positions that are not their natural berth, compromising their ability to deliver their usual late punch. A controlled, single-pace gallop on soft ground over just 5f strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong without needing a strong end-to-end gallop to set up a finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prompt Track
scenarios.trigger: If Black Missile sets an uncontested honest gallop and the tracking prominent types get a clean passage to challenge at the 1f pole.
scenarios.body: Black Missile dictates the fractions and is never seriously pressured, leaving Act Of Violence, Toptime and Overbudget able to travel smoothly just off the pace and mount their challenge from a race-fit position; on soft ground over 5f, early cover and a prominent pitch is the most efficient route to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Black Missile gets particularly loose in front on a slow surface and the rest fail to close the gap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Julie Camacho's three-year-old, equipped with a visor, sets fractions that prove beyond the field on ground that rewards relaxed travel and economical racing; the prominent tracking horses cannot pick up sufficiently and Black Missile holds on under Rossa Ryan.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the ground plays considerably slower than expected, creating a late-race crawl that allows the redistributed midfield horses to close.
scenarios.body: Knicks or Sergeant Mayer, though racing out of their natural hold-up role, are talented enough at this trip to produce a late rattle if the pace unexpectedly relents; however both carry a significant style-fit discount given their repositioned map placement and neither is a true late finisher in this configuration.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely fast and the field cracks late, opening a gap for a true closer to weave through.
scenarios.body: Staniel Cay and Ezra Cee are the genuine hold-up types with the clearest soft-ground profiles, but with so many closers forced into mid-division this scenario requires a near-perfect trip and a stronger pace than Black Missile is likely to generate alone; this is the least probable outcome given the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Black Missile and Rossa Ryan — if they steal an uncontested lead on the turn-in, the field's prominent trackers must react immediately or risk conceding a gap that a 5f Soft-ground trip will not allow them to close.|

Knicks, Jojo Rabbit, Sergeant Mayer and Just King High are all genuine hold-up horses who cannot simultaneously find their natural positions — watch for early scrimmaging and traffic problems as they jockey for limited rear-field space.|

Toptime is the prominent tracker with the most directly relevant soft-ground winning form (won on Soft 23 days ago over this trip); if Alistair Rawlinson can slot in second or third early, monitor whether that form translates under a rise in class.|

Act Of Violence carries Silvestre De Sousa's booking — a significant jockey upgrade for Tony Carroll's yard — and is prominent by style; watch whether De Sousa elects to press Black Missile or sit a length off, as that tactical decision shapes the final furlong entirely.|

Going description for this race is listed as Good to Soft throughout the card — not the Soft declared in race conditions — so if the ground plays firmer than anticipated, the advantage shifts slightly away from hold-up finishers and toward the prominent, pace-controlling profile.|

races.name: Quality Freight Services Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Harry's Halo
runners_data.note: Consistent soft-ground performer (1W9P in similar conditions) for Kevin & Lauren Frost, Jack Mitchell in the saddle — a genuine hold-up horse who wants a strong gallop to aim at, and the restrained tempo Court Alert is likely to set may not fully suit; 8 days since last run is a plus.|

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's veteran (7yo) has five consecutive 6f runs in good-to-good soft conditions but without a win, suggesting he finds a way to be competitive without ever finding that final gear; Rossa Ryan takes over and the improved jockey booking is the main flag.|

runners_data.name: Trust Amy
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's 3yo was last seen 4 days ago and bounces quickly, with form showing a 3rd on soft at 6f — Grace McEntee rides and the horse's hold-up style means everything depends on whether the leader fades early enough to be caught; the rapid turnaround needs monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Brazen Idol
runners_data.note: John Ryan's 7yo is a confirmed hold-up horse whose natural rear-of-field style has been pushed into a midfield slot on the map because the field is loaded with closers; Sean D Bowen is an upgrade in class, and the horse's best soft form came at 5f (2nd on good), making 6f on today's going a slight query.|

runners_data.name: Yachtsman
runners_data.note: Jack Morland's 3yo won a 6f good-ground race recently and has form at this trip — Jonny Peate rides and the horse's prominent-to-hold-up profile means it could slot in just behind Court Alert and be ideally placed if the leader sets a sedate pace; no soft-ground evidence is the sole caveat.|

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse shuffled toward midfield on the map — Edward Smyth-Osbourne's 3yo has run exclusively on good ground (0W0P on soft by sim-going measure) and that absence of soft-ground form is a meaningful concern today; Alistair Rawlinson rides.|

runners_data.name: Court Alert
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 3yo is the lone front-runner — Charles Bishop partners and the horse's style should allow it to slide into an uncontested lead; the Style_Fit flag reflects that it will be racing in an uncharacteristically prominent role relative to its broader profile, and good-ground form dominates its record.|

runners_data.name: Arctic Wind
runners_data.note: David Evans's 3yo has placed twice on soft (3rds at 5f) and is a natural hold-up horse repositioned closer on the map due to the field's makeup — Rob Hornby has course-and-distance experience, and any early tactical dash to secure a better pitch would be a role reversal that may not suit this patient type.|

runners_data.name: Valentine Catcher
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 5yo — yard in excellent form (14/87 in 14 days) — has placed on soft at 6f and brings proven going credentials; a true hold-up horse whose map position overstates its likely early race berth, and Jake Dickson's 5lb claim could offset any positional disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Nebbia
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's 3yo has been beaten late in sprint company and its natural hold-up style is shown in midfield only because the map is congested with closers — David Egan is a high-quality booking, and the horse's best form came at 5f on good ground, making the 6f on soft a compound query.|

runners_data.name: Tomarlo
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 4yo returns after 54 days — the longest layoff in the field — and while Stevie Donohoe knows the horse well, the absence combined with form that suggests soft-ground (0W1P) is merely tolerated rather than loved makes this a speculative runner despite the soft-going tick-box on trip.|

runners_data.name: Trust Sergei
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's second runner (alongside Trust Amy) — a 4yo with wins on standard and fast going but no soft form, natural hold-up style pushed into an artificial midfield slot; Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim is the headline angle, and if the race develops with a sharp early pace this low-weighted runner could outrun its odds on a flat 6f track.|

races.paceDynamic: Court Alert is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push them from the break, they should be able to control tempo from stall to the two-furlong pole on Good To Soft ground at Leicester. The soft underfoot conditions will naturally compress the pace, meaning Court Alert is unlikely to be pressured into an unsustainably fast gallop — instead they can bowl along at a measured clip that rewards those who sit just behind. The overwhelming majority of this field — Brazen Idol, Eyes Front, Arctic Wind, Valentine Catcher, Nebbia, Tomarlo and Trust Sergei — are all genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there simply is not enough front-running room for all of them; of these, Arctic Wind and Valentine Catcher have the strongest form evidence to suggest they can at least reach a prominent position if they break quickly. The race shape strongly favours closers who possess a sharp turn of foot on soft ground, and those sitting just off Court Alert's shoulder in the slipstream — the genuine prominent or early-midfield types — are best positioned to pounce as the leader's energy dissipates inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Court Alert Dictates, Late Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Court Alert leads at a controlled tempo on the soft and the field fails to close until too late.
scenarios.body: Court Alert sets a sustainable gallop on Good To Soft, and any horse able to track them in second or third without burning energy has a decisive positional advantage into the final furlong. This shape most suits a runner who can sit two lengths off the leader and quicken when the gap opens — a prominent-to-midfield profile on soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Off Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Court Alert's early pace — even if modest — proves too much for the soft ground and they fade sharply in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The energy tax of soft going catches up with any runner that has led throughout, and a wave of hold-up horses — those who genuinely settled in the rear and conserved themselves — come with a late run. On this ground at 6f, horses with proven soft-going form and finishing speed benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If one or more redistributed hold-up horses breaks fast and grabs a prominent pitch, setting up a front-three finish.
scenarios.body: A more contested early pace develops than the map suggests, with Arctic Wind or Valentine Catcher securing a closer position than their natural style would dictate, meaning the race resolves into a grinding battle between front-rank types on the soft. Soft-ground proven runners who handle a stamina test at 6f gain an edge over pure speedsters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Spreads Wide, Chaotic Shape
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of so many hold-up types causes positional scrimmaging early and the pace becomes ragged and uneven.
scenarios.body: With seven horses mapped out of their natural role, early crowding and checking can disrupt the race shape entirely, leaving it without a clear tempo blueprint and producing an unpredictable result. In this scenario, a horse that is versatile in style and can handle traffic — such as Trust Amy or Nebbia — could emerge from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Court Alert's ability to control tempo unchallenged is central to the entire race shape — if they are slow away or hustled early by Arctic Wind or Valentine Catcher grabbing a forward position, the probability distribution shifts sharply toward Scenario C.

Seven hold-up horses are operating out of their natural role today; watch for congestion and shuffling in the first furlong as Brazen Idol, Arctic Wind, Valentine Catcher and others all attempt to find positions that the race shape cannot comfortably give all of them.

Trust Amy runs for the second time in four days — monitor market moves and paddock demeanour, as rapid turnarounds on soft ground can expose a horse that has not fully recovered, particularly a lightly-raced 3yo.

The going is officially Good To Soft for this 6f race despite the soft label in the header — confirm the exact strip used at race time, as Leicester's track can vary significantly by draw and running rail position, potentially aiding low-drawn runners who get to the better ground.

Valentine Catcher's trainer Tim Easterby is striking at 14 winners from 87 runners in the past 14 days — a yard in peak form with a horse that has soft-ground placed form at 6f is worth tracking even if the horse's hold-up style is compromised by the race shape.

races.name: British Ebf W.b Simpson & Sons (midlands) Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Princess Rascal
runners_data.note: Held-up by nature and that style suits the anticipated strong pace well; wears headgear, has run creditably on soft and good-to-soft, and the return to a trip where she scored last time is a positive, though recent form figures are patchy.

runners_data.name: Gaspacho
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained three-year-old returning after 311 days off, but both career wins came on soft ground and her form figures on similar going read 1,1 — the fitness concern is real but the profile, if cherry-picked for this conditions race, is compelling.

runners_data.name: Dove Tale
runners_data.note: One of the four outright pace-setters; Gosden-trained with headgear applied, she won over 10f on Standard but faces a stiff test trying to dominate when three other confirmed front-runners will contest the early lead from flag fall.

runners_data.name: Quisana
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's reliable front-runner has been busy and consistent, winning over 8f on Good ground, but all five recent runs are on Good or Good-to-Soft and this softer surface plus the step up to 1m2f with three other leaders pressing introduces significant doubt.

runners_data.name: Queen's Companion
runners_data.note: Beckett runner with front-running profile who returns after 45 days; ran once on soft and managed only a third, and with four horses vying for the lead she is unlikely to dominate — her chance diminishes if the early pace turns combative.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Athene
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing three-year-old with two wins already this season; has handled a range of surfaces but her wins came on Good and Standard rather than soft, and Ashley Lewis's 3lb claim is a practical positive in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Lucky Luna
runners_data.note: Front-runner from the Hannon yard, just seven days since her last run and racing again quickly; best effort was a win on soft over 7f suggesting the ground is not a concern, but the step to 1m2f and three rivals equally keen to lead are genuine questions.

runners_data.name: Mother Dear
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's hold-up filly hasn't run for 70 days and returns with a short form string; her single win came over 10f on Good and she needs to show her absence hasn't blunted her, but the strong pace scenario and her hold-up style mean the race is set up structurally for her.

runners_data.name: Roman Secret
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent runner from Mullaney who is outclassed on official ratings and whose trainer's 14-day record reads 0 wins from 6; all form is on Standard surfaces, and while she placed once on similar going her overall profile makes her a long-shot in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Dove Tale, Quisana, Queen's Companion, and Lucky Luna all carry front-running profiles into a 1m2f test on Good to Soft ground, virtually guaranteeing a contested, pressured gallop from the outset with no horse able to dictate unchallenged. With four leaders scrapping for position early, the pace is set to be strong and relentless, burning through stamina reserves on softened ground and compressing the race into a demanding slog in the home straight. This scenario places a significant premium on horses who can settle off a hot pace and still produce a meaningful late effort, meaning the race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield types who can conserve energy in the early exchanges and attack when the leaders cry enough. Hold-up horses with proven soft-ground stamina are the principal beneficiaries here, with closers best positioned to exploit the inevitable fade from those who burn themselves out in the pace duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders Burn, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way pace battle combusts early and the field strings out, leaving the front-runners spent turning in.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop on soft ground will drain the leaders rapidly, leaving the closing stages open for those who have been settled and travelling in behind; soft-ground stamina becomes the defining quality with the race likely won between the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners finds a clean early position just off the pace duel and conserves enough to outstay the fading leaders.
scenarios.body: A horse who avoids the early scrimmage between the outright leaders while still travelling handy will have the best of both worlds — close enough to strike without having burnt energy fighting for position; Gaspacho, with strong soft-ground form and a prominent style, fits this profile most precisely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bolts Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one leader breaks cleanly from the others, controls a sustainable tempo, and builds an unassailable advantage before the field can organise a chase.
scenarios.body: Should Dove Tale or Quisana establish a clear lead without a war erupting behind them, the race becomes a stamina test that rewards whoever settles best in front on ground they handle; given all four leaders are equally matched for position, this outcome requires fortune in the stalls and early stride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Too Far Back
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly steadies in the middle stages and the race becomes a tactical sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run middle section would compress the field and favour those with a turn of foot rather than pure stamina; this scenario disadvantages true hold-up horses like Princess Rascal who need the race run to suit, and would promote the classier prominent types who can quicken.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a pace implosion in the first three furlongs — Dove Tale, Quisana, Queen's Companion, and Lucky Luna all want to lead, and a fierce early speed duel on soft ground could see the entire front group fade dramatically from the two-furlong pole.

Gaspacho's 311-day absence is a serious fitness flag; if William Haggas has targeted this race specifically for her soft-ground profile the market move will be telling, but a horse returning off nearly a year needs to be monitored in the betting ring and at the start.

Queen's Companion has run only once on soft going and finished third; if the ground deteriorates further through the afternoon card, her jumping-off point from all her form on firmer surfaces becomes a material concern.

Mother Dear's 70-day absence means her fitness is unproven, but Rob Hornby's booking for a Hughie Morrison filly is a positive signal — watch for her to be produced with a wide, late run if the pace is as strong as expected.

Roman Secret's presence at a markedly lower OR (57 vs field average ~75) means she is a potential pace contributor from a prominent position; if she helps drive the tempo alongside the confirmed leaders, the benefit flows directly to the hold-up horses at the rear.

races.name: Your Move Estate Agents Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forca Timao
runners_data.note: Mark Pattinson's six-year-old has zero wins and zero places from 15 similar-going runs, which is a deeply concerning statistic; Alfie Redman's 5lb claim is modest compensation and, though the horse genuinely races from the rear, the pace shape here offers virtually no scenario in which a true closer can build enough momentum to threaten.

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: Hope Regan's 7lb claim helps offset the 135lb burden, but Stipulation has placed just once in five runs on Good-or-better ground and his form has been consistently mid-to-rear in the field; a hold-up type who will need the pace to collapse late, which on this shape looks structurally unlikely.

runners_data.name: Jewel Maker
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard has been busy (14 runners in 14 days) and the 11-year-old is fresh off a 9f win 12 days ago on Good ground, which is the standout recent winning piece of form in the race; he typically races from the hold-up position and will need Jake Dickson's 3lb claim to count, but the softer ground stretches his stamina-based assets.

runners_data.name: Ricardo Phillips
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's five-year-old has won and placed multiple times at 10f and 12f on Good and Standard, giving him strong trip credentials; his natural style is to race from the rear but with so many closers in this field he is likely to be squeezed into a midfield berth — a position that may actually suit the race shape better than his ideal.

runners_data.name: Merapi
runners_data.note: Four consecutive placed finishes at 8f-10f show a horse in good heart, and the 103-day break is the one flag to monitor; Kyle McHugh's claim is useful, and while Merapi's instinct is to close from off the pace, the congested hold-up group means he may end up racing in third or fourth where his cruising speed is an asset rather than a liability.

runners_data.name: Cy Twombly
runners_data.note: John Mackie's four-year-old has finished in the top four just once in five recent starts on Standard ground and his form string of 098940 offers little encouragement; Finlay Bassett's 7lb claim is helpful but the horse's television-headgear suggests a mind-management issue and his overall profile marks him as one of the weaker chances regardless of how the race is run.

runners_data.name: Little Tiger
runners_data.note: William Stone's six-year-old has won and placed on similar going and his form at 10f is solid enough, but the redistribution into midfield means he cannot sit where he would naturally prefer; Laura Coughlan rides without an apprentice allowance and the horse's best form was on more testing surfaces, making him a minor player in the most probable race shape.

runners_data.name: Knightmare
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here, she will have first run on the field from stall placement and her record of five placings in six starts underlines consistency; soft-ground form is not proven but her six-day turnaround suggests the trainer David Evans is confident, and Miss Amy Tucker's 7lb claim eases the burden at the top of this particular shape.

runners_data.name: Withoutfurtherado
runners_data.note: Only nine days since last run and the 5-0597 form string reveals inconsistency at shorter distances; Liam Wright rides without a claim and, though the horse's natural position is at the rear, the race shape gives him nothing to aim at — the best the yard connection (Charalambous & Clutterbuck) can realistically hope for is a tidy but uncompetitive midfield finish.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's six-year-old has placed at 10f and 12f on multiple occasions and his form string of 762233 suggests a horse that finds the frame regularly without winning; Jack Callan rides without a claim but Charencey's quiet consistency at longer distances means he remains a each-way threat if connections manage to find him a position just behind the pace rather than deep in the pack.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's four-year-old has won at 8f on Soft and placed twice at 10f, so the going is not an issue and the trip is within range; William Pyle rides, and while the horse is a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield by the traffic, a form figure of 4 last time at 8f on Soft gives a small fragment of hope that softer conditions could coax out a better run than the overall record suggests.

races.paceDynamic: Knightmare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push her along, meaning she can dictate a measured, unhurried tempo on the Soft ground over 1m2f at Leicester. With the pace report confirming Good to Soft conditions throughout the card, the going will reward stamina and controlled rhythm rather than speed, and Knightmare's recent form string of 222125 — including a course win over 8f — shows she handles these surfaces and loves to bowl along in front. The absence of any pressuring lead horse means she is likely to produce a steadily-run affair that only quickens in the straight, compressing the race into a short dash home and giving hold-up horses very little time or distance to make their ground from the rear. This shape overwhelmingly favours prominent or just-off-the-pace runners who can travel within a length or two of Knightmare through the race and pounce as the pace lifts; true hold-up horses will find the late charge too short and too congested. Note that the field holds far more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate — Ricardo Phillips, Merapi, Cy Twombly, Little Tiger, Withoutfurtherado, Charencey and Dinah Myte are all genuine closers who will be forced to race closer to midfield than their natural position; of these, Ricardo Phillips and Merapi, with their stronger form claims and prominent-race histories, are most likely to actually secure the better tracking positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Knightmare Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Knightmare breaks well and is allowed to control a modest pace throughout, meeting no pressure from the field.
scenarios.body: Knightmare rolls along in front on her own terms, the tempo stays compressed and the race is run in her favour all the way to the home straight where her familiarity with holding a lead proves decisive; any horse inclined to sit just behind her — likely Ricardo Phillips or Merapi pushed forward from their natural style — gets a dream run in second or third.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the redistributed hold-up types — especially Ricardo Phillips or Merapi — secure a handy tracking position and produce a strong finish as the pace quickens.
scenarios.body: Ricardo Phillips has won over this trip on Good ground and his form string of 93-321 shows a horse capable of finishing strongly when delivered at the right moment; Merapi has placed twice at 10f and twice at 9f and, if his jockey Kyle McHugh pushes him forward to sit third or fourth, he is the most dangerous finisher in the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Slog Test
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides considerably more testing than the Good to Soft going report suggests, turning the race into a gruelling stamina test that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: In a true stamina contest the extra reserves of older, more experienced horses who have already won or placed on soft-ish ground come to the fore; Jewel Maker, at 11 years old but with a recent win at 9f on Good, and Charencey, who has placed at 10f and 12f consistently, hold the sounder staying credentials to handle a real slog.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Knightmare gets caught up in early traffic or overcooks the early fractions, opening a window for genuine hold-up finishers to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: Given most closers in this field are pushed out of their natural position and forced to race midfield, a truly late run is structurally unlikely; only Forca Timao or Stipulation, who are confirmed rear-of-field types, could benefit, but neither has the form to suggest they can make up the required ground in the straight on soft going.

watchPoints.text: Knightmare's early break is critical — if Miss Amy Tucker allows her to stride straight into a rhythm unchallenged from the gate, the race could be over as a contest by halfway on this soft ground and compressed tempo.

Monitor Ricardo Phillips's early position: if Harry Vigors (3lb claim) pushes him forward into third or fourth in the first furlong, he moves from a marginal hope into a genuine danger, as his form at this trip on similar ground is the strongest in the field.

Merapi's 103-day absence is the key query for Kyle McHugh — a blow-out race returning from a long break is possible, but if he travels smoothly through midfield in the first half of the race it signals he is ready to fire and should be upgraded.

The going may ride more testing than reported — all seven earlier races were recorded as Good to Soft, but a 1m2f trip late in the card on soft ground in October can accumulate significantly more cut, which would particularly benefit horses with proven soft-ground stamina records like Dinah Myte and Jewel Maker.

With so many hold-up horses compressed into midfield, early position disputes in the first two furlongs are plausible — watch for any rider forced to check or switch, as the first bend at Leicester over 1m2f arrives quickly and a poor start will cost ground that cannot be recovered in a slowly-run race.
